summary:
This law asks the Secretary of the Interior to allow special displays in Washington, D.C., for the 250th birthday of the United States. The Secretary of the Interior is the government leader who helps manage national parks and monuments.

The displays would happen on and near the National Mall. They could include objects, digital pictures, films, sound, and other images about the 250th anniversary of the United States. Some of the display could be projected onto the Washington Monument.

This would be a one-time event. It would take place during the period from December 31, 2025, to January 5, 2026. The public display on the Washington Monument would last for 5 nights.

The law says this date is important because New Year’s Eve 2025 begins the year leading up to July 4, 2026, which is 250 years after the Declaration of Independence.

The law also asks the Clerk of the House to send an official copy of this resolution to the Secretary of the Interior and to the Chair of the United States Semiquincentennial Commission, the group planning the 250th anniversary events.
